P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Partly restricted. Individual current-account FX transactions are convertible, but individuals' FX sales (settlement into RMB) and purchases are each managed under an annual facilitation quota of USD 50,000 per person. Within the quota, banks process with ID only; above it, the authenticity of transactions is examined and supporting documents (e.g. contracts) are needed. SAFE monitors split transactions through a bank-SAFE information system.

sources.quote: Q: It is stipulated in the recently promulgated Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange that management of an annual quota shall be applicable to individual foreign exchange sales and domestic individual foreign exchange purchases, and it is specified in the Detailed Rules that the respective annual quota shall be USD 50,000.

sources.title: SAFE Q&A on the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: The usual vehicle is an individual industrial and commercial household (个体工商户), registered with the market regulation authority. Only Chinese citizens, including permanent residents of Hong Kong and Macau and residents of Taiwan, may register one; foreigners cannot. E-commerce operators must register as market entities. Exceptions cover small sporadic transactions; under the 2021 Measures, individuals with cumulative annual online transactions up to RMB 100,000 need not register. Exempt operators must still register for tax once tax obligations arise and must display their exemption status.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Residents (domiciled, or present 183+ days in a tax year) are taxed on worldwide income. Freelance labour-service remuneration is part of 'comprehensive income', taxed at 3%–45% on an annual basis. Income from individual businesses or sole proprietorships is taxed at 5%–35% (5% up to CNY 30,000, 35% above CNY 500,000). Foreigners resident fewer than six consecutive years are subject to special rules on foreign-source income.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: The VAT Law and its Implementation Regulations took effect on 1 January 2026. Small-scale taxpayers, generally those under RMB 5m annual sales, pay 3%, reduced to 1% until 31 December 2027. From 2026 to 2027 there is a statutory exemption for monthly sales of RMB 100,000 (quarterly RMB 300,000); whether exactly RMB 100,000 is inclusive is unclear. Qualifying exported services consumed entirely outside China (e.g. R&D, design and software services) are zero-rated for eligible taxpayers.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL), in force since 1 November 2021, works alongside the Cybersecurity Law and the Data Security Law. It has extraterritorial reach, and outbound transfers are subject to security-assessment rules. For serious violations, fines are up to RMB 50 million or 5% of annual revenue, plus possible business suspension.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under Article 25 of the Consumer Rights Protection Law, consumers may return goods bought online, by TV, telephone or mail order within 7 days of receipt without giving a reason. Exceptions include custom-made goods, perishables, downloaded or unsealed digital products, and newspapers. Sellers must refund within 7 days of receiving the return; return shipping is borne by the consumer unless agreed otherwise. E-commerce operators must display licence or exemption information (E-Commerce Law art. 15).

sources.title: What is the 7-day unconditional return policy?
sources.quote: According to Article 25, Chapter III, of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests, consumers have the right to return products purchased through online shopping, television shopping, telephone shopping and postal shopping within 7 days (starting from the day they receive the product) without providing any reason.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Fully localized'). (5) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
